verdict: ULAM'S METHOD APPLIED TO PERTURBATION SPREAD. The premise checks out: the response-size distribution is heavy-tailed (log-log slope -1.41 against critical Galton-Watson's -1.5), massively over-dispersed (Fano 91.3 where Poisson is 1.0), and 689/1400 knockouts have exactly zero specific movers, which is what extinction looks like. The cross-section is real and measurable: P(PPI partner moves | gene knocked out) = 0.00941 against a 0.00150 background, 6.26x enrichment. THE MULTIPLICATION FACTOR IS R0 = 0.72, SUBCRITICAL, and the formula matters: the naive p*<k> gives 0.25, but a node reached BY an edge is size-biased, so the correct branching number uses the EXCESS degree <k^2>/<k>-1 = 76.2. Equivalently p/p_c = 0.72. Subcritical-but-near-critical is exactly the regime that produces heavy tails and frequent extinction, so the model and the observed distribution agree on the qualitative picture. MONTE CARLO IS NOT USABLE AT PER-GENE RESOLUTION HERE, AND THIS WAS TESTED FIRST, BEFORE ANY PERFORMANCE NUMBER. Two independent runs at 3000 replicates agree with each other at Spearman 0.276 -- the estimator does not reproduce ITSELF -- while agreeing with the cheap linear walk at 0.419. So the MC-vs-linear disagreement is sampling noise, not nonlinearity. The arithmetic is elementary: at R0 = 0.72 the reachability probabilities are ~1e-4, so at 3000 replicates most genes are hit zero or one times and the ranking is Poisson noise. THIS IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE FROM THE PREVIOUS TWO Monte Carlos in this repo, which were rank-decorative; this one is statistically infeasible, and the distinction matters because it says WHERE MC can still work. SO THE MC IS SPENT WHERE ULAM SPENT IT: ON THE AGGREGATE. He never computed the probability that a particular neutron reached a particular place; he computed the multiplication factor. An aggregate over ~10^4 genes has a relative standard error smaller by sqrt(n). The aggregate here is the BLAST RADIUS, the number of genes a knockout moves, which is the direct neutron-count analogue and is measured and held out. Baseline ladder, Spearman against the true count over all 1400 knockouts in 5-fold CV: train mean -0.0401, PPI degree alone 0.3135, essentiality alone 0.4286, a GBM on node features 0.4325, the analytic mean-field cascade alone 0.3171, node-GBM plus the cascade 0.4120 (-0.0204 over the GBM without it), and adding the MC moments 0.3957 (-0.0163). THE CASCADE FEATURE DOES NOT BEAT THE NODE FEATURES IT IS BUILT FROM. A branching simulation that cannot beat degree-plus-essentiality in a GBM has demonstrated nothing beyond restating degree, and that is the honest reading of -0.0204. AND THE MC MOMENTS ADD -0.0163 ON TOP, with the cascade SD correlating with the cascade mean at +0.975 and P(zero) at -0.922 -- not perfectly monotone, so they are not merely the mean in disguise. WHAT THIS CANNOT SAY. Only 674 of 15,183 specific movers (4.4%) are direct PPI partners of the knocked-out gene, so a cascade on this graph could never have explained WHICH genes move -- it was only ever testable on HOW MANY, which is why blast radius is the target. The cross-section is measured at hop 1, from a gene that was destroyed, and then applied at hops 2-3 where the source is merely perturbed; that is the same assumption Ulam made in reusing one cross-section at every collision, but it is far less safe here, and it would bias R0 upward. CRISPRi knockdown is partial (median 42.8% transcript remaining), so 'knocked out' is itself an idealisation. Evaluation is all 1400 knockouts, deliberately NOT the 378 scorable ones, because filtering on >=5 movers would condition the evaluation set on the target being predicted.
